construct: Activated GPCRs can be phosphorylated by G-protein-coupled receptor kinases (GRKs), which promotes β-arrestin binding. β-arrestin sterically uncouples the receptor from its G protein and facilitates clathrin-dependent internalization; prolonged stimulation can produce receptor downregulation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Persistent agonist activation causes GRK phosphorylation of activated GPCRs, recruitment of β-arrestin, receptor-G-protein uncoupling, and later internalization.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Changes in downstream cAMP metabolism could alter response amplitude, but the stem documents receptor phosphorylation before internalization and asks for homologous receptor desensitization.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The receptor-localized temporal sequence uniquely supports GRK phosphorylation followed by β-arrestin binding.
